thread.title: UPDATE: Why the bloodletting in FAANG stocks is just getting started: Canaccord

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: Why the bloodletting in FAANG stocks is just getting started: Canaccord
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
Hide behind defensives? That doesn't seem like such a crazy strategy lately as investors wait to see if worries about the U.S. economy turn into real problems in the coming year.
Tuesday's session offered the most recent evidence of that as health care, consumer staples and utilities drove the gains for the S&P 500. Compare these numbers--the Utilities Select Sector SPDR (XLU) is up 4% for the quarter, while the Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) has slumped over 12%.
Read: Utility stocks have beaten the S&P 500 in two months of turbulence and in the long run (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/utility-stocks-have-beaten-the-sp-500-in-two-months-of-turbulence-and-in-the-long-run-2018-11-28)
Another burning question for investors is whether the bloodletting has stopped for shooting-star growth names--Facebook (FB) , (AAPL), Amazon (AMZN), Netflix (NFLX) and Google-parent Alphabet (GOOGL)--which have been shoved into bear territory after helping to drive a nearly decadelong bull market.
Our call of the day from analysts at Canaccord says stay hunkered down. They see the outperformance for defensives as just getting started, because FAANG underperformance is also in its early innings.
Defense stocks were supposed to be the story for 2019 but have stepped up to the plate early because big value sectors--financials and energy--didn't, say Canaccord's Martin Roberge and Guillaume Arseneau.
Portfolio managers haven't seen any big hurt when it comes to that group of growthy stocks because year-to-date, some of those tech-focused names are still outperforming the market, they note. Beaten-down Apple is still up nearly 3% year-to-date, against a 0.3% rise for the S&P.
"We expect the real pain will come when a clear rotation occurs. This rotation should get under way when it becomes clear that earnings growth for FAANGs and other technology names in 2019 do not live up to expectations," said the Canaccord analysts. And that second wave of selling should start in January when fourth-quarter results start rolling out, they say.
Last word goes to hedge-fund manager Mark Yusko, who likens this year's stock pullback to a "melting ice cube."
"I think next year, with the economic slowdown, it gets worse--probably double-digit drawdown. The big year is 2020, when the credit bubble starts to blow up," as companies that have been binging on cheap debt will have to pay the piper,the founder and CEO of Morgan Creek Capital told CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/11/27/mark-yusko-who-called-recent-rout-says-selling-just-getting-started.html).
The market
Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures are firmer, with all eyes on a speech from Fed Chairman Jerome Powell due later. The S&P , Dow and Nasdaq all closed higher on Tuesday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-set-to-pull-back-as-trump-says-highly-unlikely-he-would-hold-off-on-raising-china-tariffs-2018-11-27).
Crude , the dollar and gold are also pretty flat.

The chart
Down 20% with just three sessions left in November, Apple (AAPL) is on track for its worth month since the week ending Sept. 30, 2008, when markets were in the grip of the financial crisis and the iPhone maker endured a 32% plunge. See just below for that sobering chart of the day:
"Apple has become synonymous with the macro narrative, a state of affairs that compounds its already outsize sway over the broader market," notes the anonymous blogger behind The Heisenberg Report (https://heisenbergreport.com/2018/11/27/rotten-apple-when-one-company-becomes-synonymous-with-the-macro-story/).
The blogger also points out this cold-comfort chart, that shows how the 10-day correlation between Apple and the S&P 500 is at the highest of 2018:
The buzz
In a wide-ranging interview with the Washington Post, POTUS laid into Fed Chief Powell-- (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-again-lashes-out-at-powell-says-hes-not-even-a-little-bit-happy-about-naming-him-fed-chief-2018-11-27) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-again-lashes-out-at-powell-says-hes-not-even-a-little-bit-happy-about-naming-him-fed-chief-2018-11-27)due to speak at noon--saying he wasn't "even a little bit happy with my selection of Jay," and blaming him for Wall Street's woes. Trump also (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-again-lashes-out-at-powell-says-hes-not-even-a-little-bit-happy-about-naming-him-fed-chief-2018-11-27)threatened to cancel a meeting at the G-20 this weekend with Russian President Vladimir Putin over a clash between that country and Ukraine.
In a separate interview with Politico (https://www.politico.com/story/2018/11/28/trump-politico-interview-1023306), Trump said he'd shut down the government over border-wall funding.
Salesforce (CRM) is popping higher after the software company's earnings and its outlook beat forecasts (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/salesforces-stock-surges-after-earnings-beat-fiscal-2020-revenue-outlook-2018-11-27). The cloud company could be a haven in a potential tech storm (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/forecasts-see-no-dark-clouds-on-horizon-for-salesforce-nutanix-2018-11-27).
Tiffany (TIF) is sliding on results and Burlington (BURL) is up after lifting its earnings outlook.
Just months after launching, YouTube--owned by Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google--is reportedly pulling back on its premium subscription service (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/youtube-reportedly-scaling-back-its-premium-tier-for-original-content-2018-11-27).
Cannabis company Curaleaf tanked in Canada after posting a substantial loss (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/marijuana-producer-curaleaf-revenue-nearly-triples-in-first-earnings-after-public-listing-2018-11-27).
Former Facebook (FB) worker, Mark S. Luckie, says his company is "failing black employees and its black users," as he spoke of widespread discrimination at the social media company in a letter he made public (https://www.facebook.com/notes/mark-s-luckie/facebook-is-failing-its-black-employees-and-its-black-users/1931075116975013/).
